items.item: Each row shows the user's name and email, role, status in words (such as Active, Invited, Deactivated, Locked) and whether two-factor sign-in is enabled
items.evidence: renderRows() (page.html:592-612) outputs name, email, role, and a word status badge via statusBadge() (only Active/Invited/Deactivated tones defined, no Locked state). There is no column, icon, or text anywhere for two-factor/MFA status — no '2FA', 'two-factor', or 'MFA' string exists in the page.

items.item: Last sign-in uses one date-time format with the timezone stated, relative times also expose the exact time, and an account that has never signed in shows "Never" rather than a blank or a 1970 date
items.evidence: formatDateTime() (page.html:317-321) uses `d.toLocaleString("en-US", {month:'short', day:'numeric', year:'numeric', hour:'numeric', minute:'2-digit'})` — no timeZone/timeZoneName option, so no timezone is ever stated (screenshot shows 'Nov 7, 2026, 8:42 AM · today' with no TZ abbreviation). The exact time and relative time are shown together ('today', '1d ago' next to the date), and `lastSignInCell` falls back to 'Never' when lastSignIn is null (page.html:597-599) — but the missing timezone fails the item.

items.item: Users can be found by searching name or email and filtered by role, status and inactivity (such as no sign-in for 90+ days), with the number of matching users shown
items.evidence: getFiltered() (page.html:383-394) filters by search text over name+email, by state.roles, and by state.statusTab, and #result-count shows 'N of M users' (page.html:668). There is no inactivity/last-sign-in-age filter anywhere in state, getFiltered(), or the filter bar markup — no '90' or 'inactive' logic exists.

items.item: The invite form requires an email and a role, labels both fields, and shows an inline error for a malformed address or one that already has an account
items.evidence: Invite dialog labels Email (`<label for="invite-email">Email`) and Role (`<label for="invite-role">Role`), and validateEmail() (page.html:1125-1131) shows an inline error for empty or regex-failing addresses ('Enter an email like name@company.com'). However there is no duplicate-email check — submit handler (page.html:1162-1176) only checks EMAIL_RE and always creates a new user, never comparing against existing USERS emails, so 'already has an account' is never detected or shown.

items.item: Deactivation asks for confirmation that names the user and states the effect (active sessions ended, sign-in blocked, data kept), and a deactivated user is offered Reactivate instead
items.evidence: confirmDialog title 'Deactivate account for " + u.name + "?' names the user, and body states "They'll immediately lose access and be signed out of all active sessions" (sessions ended + sign-in blocked), but never states that data is kept/retained (page.html:774-785). Reactivate IS offered for Deactivated rows via rowActionsHtml's `data-action="reactivate"` button (page.html:578-579), but the missing data-retention statement fails this item.

items.item: The signed-in administrator's own row is marked (such as "You") and cannot be deactivated or lose the admin role, and the last remaining administrator cannot be deactivated, with the disabled action explaining why
items.evidence: No session/current-admin concept exists anywhere in state or USERS; rowActionsHtml() and handleRowAction() apply the identical Deactivate flow to every Active user including all three Administrators (Olivia Harper, Liam Chen, Sofia Martinez), with no self-row marker ('You'), no role-lock, and no disabled/explained state for the last admin.

items.item: Password reset sends a reset link to the user's email address, which the confirmation names, and the administrator never sees, sets or types the new password
items.evidence: handleRowAction: `showToast("Password reset link sent to " + u.email)` (page.html:766) names the specific recipient email address in the confirmation toast; there is no password input field anywhere in the invite, confirm, or row-action UI, so the admin never sets/types/sees a password.

items.item: Row actions are buttons or a keyboard-operable menu whose accessible names include the user (such as "Actions for Mai Nguyen"), and the outcome of an action is announced in an aria-live or role="status" region
items.evidence: Only the overflow-menu trigger carries a per-user accessible name: `aria-label="Actions for " + escapeHtml(u.name)` (page.html:584). The primary inline action buttons ('Reset password', 'Resend invite', 'Reactivate', page.html:568-579) have no aria-label and no user reference, so their accessible name is just the visible text (e.g. 'Reset password') with no indication of which user/row it targets. Outcome announcements do work: showToast() elements use `role="status"` (page.html:978) and #live-status is `role="status"` (page.html:138).

items.item: A search with no matching users shows a message with a way to clear it, and loading and failed-load states with a retry exist
items.evidence: noResultsHtml() shows 'No users match "term"' plus a '#no-results-clear' 'Clear filters' button (page.html:543-552); skeletonRows()/aria-busy drive the loading state (page.html:523-529, 622-630); errorStateHtml() shows "Couldn't load users" with an '#error-retry' 'Retry' button (page.html:554-563, 644-656).

notes: This screen is relatively free of the common template tells (no greeting-header, no KPI tiles, no gradients/glass, no oversized radii, no navy-sidebar-indigo-accent, no emoji icons — all icons are inline SVG, and the person-initial avatars (e.g. 'OH', 'ZT') are for real users so don't count as initials-avatar-non-person). Audit.json flags real but secondary issues: text-contrast failures (2.56:1) on the '· Xd ago' relative-time text (25 occurrences) and missing mailto: links on emails (25 occurrences) — both corroborate the last-sign-in formatting gap and the missing-identity-on-row-actions pattern noted above. Biggest structural gaps vs the checklist: no two-factor status anywhere, no timezone on timestamps, no inactivity (90+ day) filter, no duplicate-email check on invite, no 'data kept' language on deactivation, and no self/last-admin protection at all.
